reasoning: This extract is almost entirely a descriptive specification: it sets out what students must learn (lines on objectives, themes, skills), what grammar must be assumed or tested, what literary/film works must be studied, and special rules for Chinese -- but at no point does it explain why this particular delivery structure (two themes at AS, four at A level; specific grammar lists; the Chinese exception requiring English-language questions) was chosen, what alternatives were considered, or what costs/benefits were weighed. The three core themes bear this out: 'Special Provisions for Chinese Language' simply asserts rules ('Questions and responses...must be in English') without any stated rationale or evidence; 'Grammar and Language Structure - General' asserts that GCSE grammar 'is assumed' and that awarding bodies must produce comparable lists for other languages, again with no evidence of why this comparability method was chosen; 'Specification Framework' asserts that AS/A level 'must build on' GCSE content and be 'an integrated study,' again a bare assertion. No statistics, research findings, named reports, consultation responses, or comparator policies appear anywhere in the extract to justify these design choices. The strongest counter-example would be if the Chinese exception reflected consultation evidence, but none is shown. To reach level 1, the document would need to mention, even without citation, some evidence (e.g. 'research/consultation showed candidates struggled with X') explaining why these specific delivery choices -- the two-tier theme structure, the grammar lists, the Chinese exception -- were made.
